title: ie says /ie/
parentNote: Today two letters team up to say one sound, and the sound is a letter's name: ie says "eye", as in pie. That is the hard part. Your child has spent fifty days reading i as the short sound in pin, so pie usually comes out as three separate sounds — "p-i-uh" — or the i gets said short and the e gets said too. Cover the e with your finger, say the i short the old way, then slide your finger off and say the whole word: two letters, one sound, and it is over as soon as they see the pair as a pair. Point at ie as one chunk every time. This is also the door into tomorrow, when a silent e on the end does the same job to a vowel further back in the word.

activities.mouthCue: Your mouth drops open wide, then slides shut into a smile. Two mouth shapes, one sound.
activities.prompt: Two letters standing together. They do not say i and then e. Together they say eye.

activities.title: The pie and the flies
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Meg did set a big pie up on the step.
Ten flies did land on it and did not get off.
Meg cries and cries but the flies did not shift.
Ted got a red tie and did flap it at the flies.
The flies went up in the skies and Ted did grin.
Meg and Ted sat on the step and did munch the pie with fries.
